candidate.answerReason: The rhombus diagonals have lengths 6−2√3 and 2√3−2. Half their product is 8√3−12.

methods.label: Find the two diagonals
methods.explanation:
Place the square so that the triangle bases are its bottom and top sides, and let its side length be \(s=2\sqrt3\). Finding the rhombus diagonals will give its area.

The altitude of an equilateral triangle bisects its base. Thus, for side length \(t>0\), the Pythagorean theorem gives altitude
\[
\sqrt{t^2-(t/2)^2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}t.
\]
Each large triangle therefore has altitude
\[
\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(2\sqrt3)=3.
\]
Let \(P\) be the tip of the triangle with the bottom base, and let \(Q\) be the tip of the triangle with the top base. Both lie on the perpendicular line through the base midpoints. Their heights above the bottom side are \(3\) and \(s-3\), respectively. Since \(3<s<6\), each tip lies inside the other triangle, and they are opposite vertices of the intersection rhombus. Hence one diagonal has length
\[
d=PQ=3-(s-3)=6-2\sqrt3.
\]
Let \(L\) and \(R\) be the other rhombus vertices, and let \(O\) be the intersection of its diagonals. Rhombus diagonals bisect each other perpendicularly, so \(PO=d/2\).

At \(P\), the rhombus inherits the original triangle's \(60^\circ\) angle. Also \(PL=PR\), so triangle \(PLR\) is equilateral. If \(b=LR\), its altitude is therefore
\[
PO=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}b=\frac d2.
\]
It follows that \(b=d/\sqrt3=2\sqrt3-2\). The rhombus area is half the product of its diagonals:
\[
\frac12(6-2\sqrt3)(2\sqrt3-2)
=8\sqrt3-12.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
